questions.text: The 50-30-20 rule for budgeting suggests allocating:
questions.explanation: A common thumb-rule: 50 % essentials, 30 % discretionary, 20 % savings.

questions.text: Portfolio Management Services (PMS) in India are regulated under:
questions.explanation: Portfolio Management Services are governed by SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, which replaced the earlier 1993 regulations.

questions.text: An ordinary annuity differs from an annuity due because payments are:
options: Made at the beginning of each period
Made at the end of each period
questions.explanation: In an ordinary annuity, payments occur at the end of each period.

questions.text: A healthy DTI ratio for households is generally below:
questions.explanation: Debt payments above one-third of income can strain cash flows.

questions.text: Index funds in the equity segment aim to:
options: Closely replicate the performance of a specified market index
questions.explanation: Index funds passively track a benchmark index like Nifty 50.

questions.text: Which of the following intermediaries must maintain arm’s-length relationships between group entities?
questions.explanation: Both AMCs and Investment Advisers must maintain arm’s-length separation from distribution or related entities to avoid conflicts.

questions.text: Which type of interest results in 'interest on interest' effect?
questions.explanation: Compound interest reinvests earned interest, generating additional earnings on it.

questions.text: For a young investor with long investment horizon and high risk appetite, which allocation tilt is generally appropriate?
options: Higher allocation to equity and growth-oriented assets
Only bank FDs and government bonds
questions.explanation: Long horizon and high risk appetite usually justify a higher allocation to equity and growth assets.

questions.text: AIFs in India are regulated under:
questions.explanation: SEBI introduced the AIF Regulations in 2012 to bring all unregistered private pools such as PE, VC and hedge funds under a regulatory framework.

questions.text: A key ethical principle in handling client money is:
options: Mixing client funds with personal funds for convenience
Segregation of client assets from advisor’s own assets
Using client funds temporarily for personal needs
Pledging client holdings for advisor’s loans
questions.explanation: Client assets must always be segregated and never used for personal or business needs of the advisor.

questions.text: SME platforms on stock exchanges are designed for:
options: Small and medium enterprises seeking equity capital
questions.explanation: SME platforms enable smaller companies to raise equity in a lighter regulatory framework.

questions.text: The simplest measure of portfolio return is:
questions.explanation: The holding period return (HPR) measures total return over a specific investment period including income and capital gains.

questions.text: Maximum cash investment accepted in mutual fund schemes is:
questions.explanation: SEBI allows cash investments in mutual funds up to ₹50,000 per investor per financial year with proper KYC documentation.

questions.text: Which is an example of DIRECT investment by a retail investor?
options: Buying a diversified equity mutual fund
Investing through a PMS in multiple stocks
Buying listed shares of a company in her own demat account
Investing in a Category II AIF
questions.explanation: Buying shares directly in a demat account is a direct investment; mutual funds, PMS and AIFs are managed/pooled vehicles.

questions.text: Which of the following is the MOST fundamental ethical duty of an Investment Adviser?
options: Acting in the best interest of the client (fiduciary duty)
questions.explanation: An IA has a fiduciary duty to always act in the best interest of the client, ahead of their own interest.

questions.text: For mutual fund investors, the first point of contact for grievances is:
options: The concerned AMC or its Registrar and Transfer Agent (RTA)
questions.explanation: Investors should first approach the AMC or its RTA; unresolved issues can then be escalated to SEBI through SCORES.

questions.text: Capital markets are primarily used for:
options: Long-term funding through equity and debt securities
Trading only in government treasury bills
questions.explanation: Capital markets provide long-term funds via equity shares, debentures, bonds, etc.

questions.text: The minimum net worth requirement for Portfolio Managers is:
questions.explanation: Under SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, a Portfolio Manager must have a minimum net worth of ₹5 crore.

questions.text: Reducing interest rate but extending tenure on loan will generally:
options: Increase EMI and reduce total interest
Reduce EMI but may increase total interest paid
Reduce both EMI and total interest
questions.explanation: Longer tenure means lower monthly payment but higher cumulative interest.

questions.text: The Registrar of Companies (RoC) is responsible for:
options: Registering companies and monitoring compliance with company law
questions.explanation: RoC registers companies and ensures they comply with provisions of the Companies Act.

questions.text: Lock-in period for investment in an Angel Fund portfolio company is at least:
questions.explanation: Investments by an Angel Fund in a portfolio company must be locked in for a minimum of three years.

questions.text: From an ethical standpoint, client complaints should be viewed as:
options: Opportunities to improve processes and trust
questions.explanation: Complaints help identify gaps and improve service quality; handling them fairly builds long-term trust.

questions.text: If monthly income is ₹1,00,000 and expenses are ₹80,000, the monthly surplus is:
An individual earns ₹12 lakh p.a., saves ₹3 lakh, and pays ₹1.2 lakh EMIs. His savings-to-income ratio is:
According to Modern Portfolio Theory, portfolio risk is best measured by:
options: Variance or standard deviation of returns
questions.explanation: Markowitz demonstrated that variance (or standard deviation) of returns is a meaningful measure of portfolio risk.

questions.text: Discretionary Portfolio Managers:
options: Execute client trades only after client approval
Have full discretion to manage funds as per the agreed mandate
Can act as mutual fund distributors
questions.explanation: Discretionary Portfolio Managers manage and invest client funds independently as per the client’s mandate.

questions.text: If an investor requires 10% return, what is the PV of ₹1,00,000 receivable after 3 years?
questions.explanation: PV = 1,00,000/(1.10)³ = 75,131 → approx 75k; adjust numbers accordingly.

questions.text: Which of the following helps investors verify whether their intermediary is SEBI-registered?
options: SEBI’s online intermediary database on its website
questions.explanation: Investors can verify intermediary registration on SEBI’s official website under the ‘Intermediaries / Market Infrastructure Institutions’ section.

questions.text: If ₹1,00,000 is invested for 2 years at 10% p.a. simple interest, the total amount at maturity will be:
In personal financial planning, "human capital" refers to:
options: Present value of all future earning capacity of an individual
questions.explanation: Human capital is the economic value of a person’s future earning capacity.

questions.text: The current standard settlement cycle in Indian equity markets is:
questions.explanation: Indian equity markets have adopted T+1 rolling settlement (trade date plus one working day).

questions.text: A callable bond is one where:
options: The investor can redeem early at a predetermined price
The issuer has the right to redeem the bond before maturity
The coupon rate changes automatically with inflation
The bond has no maturity date
questions.explanation: Callable bonds give the issuer the right to redeem the bond prematurely, usually when interest rates fall, increasing reinvestment risk for investors.

questions.text: If an investor is not satisfied with the intermediary’s response, they can approach:
questions.explanation: Investors can escalate unresolved complaints to SEBI via its online platform, SCORES.

questions.text: The formula for the Sharpe Ratio is:
options: (Portfolio Return – Risk-Free Rate) / Standard Deviation of Portfolio
questions.explanation: Sharpe Ratio = (Rp – Rf) / σp, where Rp is portfolio return, Rf is risk-free rate, and σp is portfolio’s standard deviation.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a lifestyle goal?
options: Owning a bigger car within 3 years
Paying off credit card dues this month
questions.explanation: Lifestyle goals relate to a desired standard of living, such as owning a bigger car or a better house.

questions.text: All else equal, which bond will have the highest duration?
options: Floating rate bond with frequent resets
questions.explanation: Longer maturity and lower coupons push more cash flows into the distant future, increasing duration and interest rate sensitivity.

questions.text: Bank fixed deposits (FDs) in India are insured by DICGC up to:
questions.explanation: DICGC insures bank deposits (principal plus interest) up to ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank.

questions.text: Which of these is a red flag for a potential debt trap?
options: Using secured loans for asset purchase
questions.explanation: Using new debt to repay old indicates unsustainable leverage.

questions.text: A client wanting to retire early at age 50 instead of 60 will generally need to:
options: Save more and invest more aggressively in earlier years
questions.explanation: Early retirement means fewer earning years and more retired years, requiring higher saving and often more growth-oriented investments.

questions.text: The process of finding the present value from a known future value is called:
questions.explanation: Discounting is the reverse of compounding.

questions.text: ‘Fiduciary duty’ implies that an adviser must:
options: Place client interest above their own and avoid conflicts
questions.explanation: A fiduciary must act with utmost good faith, prioritizing client interest above personal or organizational gain.

questions.text: Power of Attorney (PoA) given to an advisor allows:
options: Execution of investment instructions on behalf of client
questions.explanation: PoA allows advisors to execute transactions or operate the investment account on behalf of the client, as authorized.

questions.text: Small-cap funds are required to invest at least 65% of their total assets in:
options: Companies ranked 251 and above by market capitalisation
questions.explanation: Small-cap companies are defined as those ranked 251 onwards by full market capitalisation, and small-cap funds must invest at least 65% in them.

questions.text: Which factor affects unsystematic risk the most?
options: Company management quality and business model
questions.explanation: Unsystematic risk stems from company-specific factors such as management decisions and industry position.

questions.text: In a multi-cap fund, SEBI requires that at least 75% of assets are in equity with minimum allocation of:
options: 25% in large-cap, 25% in mid-cap, 25% in small-cap
questions.explanation: Multi-cap funds must invest at least 75% in equity-related instruments, with a minimum of 25% each in large, mid and small-cap stocks.

questions.text: Which of the following is typically classified as a REAL asset rather than a financial asset?
questions.explanation: Real estate is a tangible real asset, while FDs, equity and bonds are financial assets.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers must not accept funds or securities worth less than:
questions.explanation: The minimum threshold of ₹50 lakh applies to each client’s investment under PMS.

questions.text: Repatriable NRI investments must be made from:
questions.explanation: For repatriable investments, funds must come through NRE or FCNR accounts maintained with Indian banks.

questions.text: A put option gives the holder:
options: The right but not obligation to sell the underlying asset at a fixed price
The obligation to buy the underlying asset
The right to receive a dividend
questions.explanation: A put option gives the buyer the right to sell the underlying asset at a specified price before or on expiry.

questions.text: The SEBI (Research Analyst) Regulations were notified in:
questions.explanation: SEBI introduced the Research Analyst Regulations in 2014 to regulate research dissemination and prevent conflicts of interest.

questions.text: A 'risk-neutral' investor:
options: Demands the highest risk premium for all investments
Focuses only on expected return, ignoring risk
questions.explanation: A risk-neutral investor evaluates investments solely on expected returns without regard for risk.

questions.text: Margin money in futures trading is primarily meant to:
options: Act as a down payment for ownership
Cover potential daily losses and ensure contract performance
questions.explanation: Margins are deposits to cover potential daily losses and ensure traders honour their obligations; they are adjusted daily via mark-to-market.

questions.text: A derivative is a financial instrument whose value is derived from:
options: An underlying asset such as a stock, bond, commodity or index
questions.explanation: A derivative’s price depends on the value or performance of an underlying asset such as equity, bond, commodity, currency or index.

questions.text: If an investor receives ₹10,000 every year for 5 years, the present value at 8% p.a. is (approx.):
The 'consolidation phase' in the investor life cycle is typically when:
options: Income exceeds expenses and focus shifts to capital preservation
The investor depends entirely on investment income
The investor is gifting wealth to heirs
questions.explanation: In the consolidation phase, income exceeds expenses, and investors begin emphasizing capital preservation.

questions.text: Permanent Account Number (PAN) is mandatory for all mutual fund investments except when:
options: Aggregate investment is up to ₹50,000 per year under Micro SIPs
questions.explanation: SEBI exempts Micro SIP investors (aggregate ≤ ₹50,000 per financial year) from mandatory PAN if other KYC norms are met.

questions.text: An AIF may be set up as a trust, company, LLP or:
questions.explanation: AIFs can be established as a trust, company, limited-liability partnership or body corporate.

questions.text: Under PMLA, intermediaries must report suspicious transactions to:
questions.explanation: The Financial Intelligence Unit–India (FIU-IND) under the Ministry of Finance receives suspicious transaction reports from intermediaries.

questions.text: If volatility of the underlying asset increases, option premiums:
questions.explanation: Higher volatility raises the probability of favourable movement, increasing both call and put option premiums.

questions.text: In case of transmission without nomination, the claimant must provide:
questions.explanation: For non-nominated cases, claimant must provide a death certificate, legal heir certificate, or notarized will copy.

questions.text: Tracking monthly expenses over time helps to:
options: Identify spending patterns and areas to cut
questions.explanation: Expense tracking improves awareness and discipline.

questions.text: Ethics in investment advisory primarily relates to:
options: Moral principles that guide behaviour towards clients and markets
questions.explanation: Ethics refers to moral principles and standards that guide behaviour and decision-making, especially when dealing with client money and trust.

questions.text: Which document must a PMS provide to clients before onboarding?
questions.explanation: The PMS must furnish a Disclosure Document detailing fees, risks, related-party transactions, and performance.

questions.text: Category I AIFs generally invest in:
questions.explanation: Category I AIFs include venture-capital, SME, social-venture and infrastructure funds that create positive economic impact.

questions.text: A company’s dividend payout ratio is defined as:
options: Dividend per share ÷ earnings per share
Earnings per share ÷ dividend per share
questions.explanation: Dividend payout ratio = Dividend per share / EPS.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly lists equity shareholder rights?
options: Voting rights, dividend entitlement, right to information
Only right to capital repayment before others
questions.explanation: Shareholders enjoy voting rights, dividends (if declared), and rights to company information.

questions.text: The Security Market Line (SML) plots:
questions.explanation: The SML depicts the relationship between expected return and beta (systematic risk) under the CAPM framework.

questions.text: Speculators in derivatives markets aim to:
options: Profit from anticipated price movements in the underlying asset
Lock in exchange rates for trade
questions.explanation: Speculators take positions in derivatives to profit from expected price changes in the underlying asset.

questions.text: The Principal Officer of a Portfolio Manager must have:
options: Minimum 5 years relevant experience and valid NISM certification
At least 10 years of audit experience
A postgraduate degree in economics only
questions.explanation: The Principal Officer must have at least 5 years’ experience in portfolio management, advisory, or related activities and hold NISM certification.

questions.text: High-yield bonds are characterised by:
options: Very low default risk and low coupon
Investment-grade rating and low spread over government securities
Sub-investment grade rating and higher default risk
questions.explanation: High-yield bonds are non–investment grade and therefore carry higher default risk, compensated by higher yields.

questions.text: The Capital Market Line (CML) plots:
options: Expected return against standard deviation for efficient portfolios
Expected return against beta for all securities
questions.explanation: The CML shows the relationship between expected return and total risk (standard deviation) for efficient portfolios including the risk-free asset.

questions.text: Which of the following participants typically use derivatives to hedge?
options: Producers or investors exposed to price or rate risk
questions.explanation: Hedgers use derivatives to protect themselves against adverse movements in prices or interest rates.

questions.text: Non-discretionary Portfolio Managers:
options: Require client approval for every transaction
Can invest only in government securities
questions.explanation: Non-discretionary Portfolio Managers act based on the client’s instructions for every investment decision.

questions.text: An investor’s holding in a mutual fund is represented by:
options: Number of shares of the AMC
Number of bonds issued by the scheme
Number of units of the scheme
Amount of cash in the trust account
questions.explanation: Each investor’s holding in a mutual fund is represented in terms of units of the scheme.

questions.text: Setting exposure limits to sectors and asset classes helps to:
questions.explanation: Exposure limits prevent excessive concentration in a single sector or security, reducing portfolio risk.

questions.text: Portfolios below the efficient frontier are:
options: Sub-optimal as they offer lower return for a given risk
questions.explanation: Portfolios below the efficient frontier are inefficient because they offer less return for the same risk level.

questions.text: A person’s income and expenses both rise 10%. The savings amount:
questions.explanation: If both rise equally in % terms, the rupee surplus remains same proportion.

questions.text: A 25-year-old with no dependants and stable income is generally more suitable for which allocation?
options: Very high proportion of assets in cash only
Higher allocation to growth assets such as equity
questions.explanation: With long time horizon and low dependants, growth assets like equity can form a higher proportion of the portfolio.

questions.text: Which of the following is a key ethical expectation from a financial planner?
options: Selling products with highest commission first
Prioritising client interest over personal gains
Making investments only in related-party products
questions.explanation: Client interest must come first; conflict of interest must be avoided or disclosed adequately.

questions.text: AMFI primarily functions as:
options: A mutual fund industry self-regulatory organization (SRO)
questions.explanation: The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) is an SRO promoting investor awareness and ethical conduct among mutual funds.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about asset allocation is TRUE?
options: It has minimal impact on portfolio performance
It is the key determinant of long-term portfolio returns and risk
It focuses only on stock selection
It can be ignored once the portfolio is constructed
questions.explanation: Empirical studies show asset allocation is the major driver of a portfolio’s long-term risk and return.

questions.text: Which of the following investors are eligible to invest in AIFs?
options: Resident, NRI and foreign investors, subject to FEMA
questions.explanation: AIFs can accept investment from resident, NRI and foreign investors in compliance with FEMA and SEBI norms.

questions.text: Savings ratio is defined as:
questions.explanation: It measures the proportion of income saved each year.

questions.text: Which of the following occurs in the primary market?
options: Issue of new securities by companies to investors
Purchase of shares on the stock exchange
Sale of government securities by RBI in the secondary market
questions.explanation: The primary market facilitates the issue of new securities by companies to raise funds from investors.

questions.text: Ethical investing primarily involves:
options: Investing in sin industries for profit
Selecting investments based on personal moral principles
questions.explanation: Ethical investing filters out investments conflicting with an investor’s moral or ethical beliefs, such as gambling or tobacco.

questions.text: Debt-to-income ratio (DTI) is computed as:
options: Monthly debt obligations ÷ Gross monthly income
questions.explanation: DTI assesses ability to service debt from monthly income.

questions.text: In an EMI, the interest component:
options: Is zero in the first year
questions.explanation: As principal outstanding reduces, the interest portion of each EMI declines.

questions.text: Which of the following is the LEAST liquid asset in general?
questions.explanation: Direct real estate is typically illiquid; sale can take time and involve high transaction costs.

questions.text: In the investor life cycle, the 'accumulation phase' is characterized by:
options: High net worth and focus on capital preservation
Building assets with higher risk tolerance and long horizon
questions.explanation: In the accumulation phase, investors are early in their careers, taking higher risk to build wealth over a long horizon.

questions.text: Preferred shareholders generally have:
options: Priority over equity shareholders in dividend and liquidation but limited voting rights
Higher returns than equity in all circumstances
questions.explanation: Preference shareholders get fixed dividends and priority in liquidation but limited or no voting rights.

questions.case_text: Ajay, aged 45, wants to retire at 60. His current monthly expenses are ₹70,000, expected to rise by 6% annually. He expects 7% post-retirement returns and plans to live till 85. Inflation-adjusted corpus required is to be estimated.
